newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says EU moves will have no effect.
newsitem.headline: Iran says EU moves will have no effect.

text.p: Iranian state radio said on Tuesday decisions by the European Union about ties with Iran would fail to affect the Islamic republic because of Iran's extended relations with countries outside Europe.

"Neither attempts by the White House (to isolate Iran) nor decisions by the European Union will have any effect on the sacred government system of the Islamic Republic of Iran," state-run Tehran radio said in a commentary.

The commentary was broadcast before EU foreign ministers suspended ministerial meetings with Iran in response to a German court ruling this month that accused Tehran leaders of ordering the murder of Iranian opposition figures in Berlin.

"Our country currently enjoys excellent relations with more than 140 world states, is more confident and stable than ever and is advancing towards balanced development while expanding its ties with world states," the radio added.
It said a meeting of foreign ministers of the 10-member regional Economic Cooperation Organisation opening in Tehran on Tuesday was an example of Iran's extensive international ties.
The EU ministers meeting in Luxembourg agreed that ambassadors from the 15 member states could return to Tehran if individual countries wanted them to.
EU governments except Greece recalled their envoys for consultations after a Berlin court on April 10 accused Tehran of ordering the 1992 murder of four Kurdish dissidents.
Tehran has denied any involvement in the murders which it blamed on in-fighting between opposition groups.
The Iranian parliament's foreign relations committee on Tuesday urged the government to end all talks with the EU.

"Talks (with the EU) can only be effective and useful when, firstly, they are constructive and coupled with good intentions and, secondly, they go beyond the limits of words and slogans," the commission said in a statement carried by Iranian television monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
"Therefore, until these conditions are met, we call on the Islamic Republic of Iran's government to end such talks with the EU under whatever names they might be called," it said.
The EU has suspended its policy of critical dialogue with Iran which has involved talks with Tehran while trying to get the country to move closer to the West.
Iranian newspapers published before Tuesday's EU decision called for curbing economic ties with Europe in favour of other trade partners.

"We have to act more wisely towards Europe and act towards cutting Europe's share and role in the fields of economic and industrial ties and create the situation in which Europe could not even get the idea of striking blows against us," the daily Jomhuri Eslami said.
The English-language Tehran Times said: "In today's world which is based on competition, it is not difficult for Iran to replace its trade partners when (its) values are at stake."
Iranian media and some officials have said Tehran could turn to Asia for its trade as a result of the row with the EU.
The EU decision to allow the return of ambassadors was seen as a sign that the bloc was reluctant to damage its lucrative ties with Iran. The EU is Iran's biggest trading partner.
The United States has urged the EU to join economic sanctions Washington has imposed on Iran for alleged sponsorship of international terrorism. Iran denies the charges.
